extracted.intended_audience: researchers and authors preparing submissions to Royal Society journals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for researchers preparing and submitting manuscripts to journals published by the Royal Society, covering suitability, manuscript preparation, peer review models, open access and related author services.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-quality science
rubrics_metrics.description: We welcome submissions of high-quality science from anywhere in the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should submit work that represents high scientific quality suitable for peer review; the publisher emphasizes excellence in science as part of its mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fit to journal aims and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Please review details about each journal and its aims and scope to verify that your article is a good match.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before submission, authors must check individual journal Aims & Scope pages to ensure topical fit; submitting to the most appropriate journal increases chances of successful review and publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good standard of English
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions require a good standard of English
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts should be written in clear, publishable English; authors may need to edit or use language-editing services to meet this expectation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions ... need to meet ethical requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must review and satisfy the Royal Society's ethical policies (e.g., on human/animal research, conflicts of interest, authorship, data integrity) prior to submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author guidelines and checklists
rubrics_metrics.description: We provide detailed guidelines and checklists to help you prepare your article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the publisher's detailed author guidelines and any checklists (formatting, figures, data availability, ethical declarations) to avoid delays or desk rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format-free initial submission
rubrics_metrics.description: We offer format-free initial submission for most of our journals, so you don’t need to worry about reformatting to our reference style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For initial submission most journals accept manuscripts without strict adherence to final formatting or reference style; however, accepted manuscripts will need to be prepared according to the journal's production requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with funder mandates (e.g., Plan S)
rubrics_metrics.description: All our journals are compliant with funder mandates such as Plan S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors with funder requirements (open access, data policies) can publish in Royal Society journals while remaining compliant; check specific funder/journal procedures if required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review model: anonymization
rubrics_metrics.description: Most Royal Society journals are normally peer reviewed in a single-anonymized fashion (author names are not concealed, but referee names are), while Notes and Records and Proceedings B are double-anonymized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should check the journal-specific peer review model (single vs double anonymization) and prepare submissions accordingly (e.g., anonymize if submitting to double-anonymized journals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of peer review information (open/transparent peer review)
rubrics_metrics.description: For Royal Society Open Science, Open Biology and Proceedings B, publication of peer review information (anonymous by default unless the reviewer signs their report) is mandatory. For Proceedings A and Biology Letters, we offer authors the option to publish peer review information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should be aware which journals publish peer review histories and consent/prepare for potential transparent review; reviewers remain anonymous unless they sign their report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access publishing options and APCs
rubrics_metrics.description: Open access publishing including APC-free open access publication through Read & Publish, Subscribe to Open and our Royal Society Open Access Equity scheme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors can publish open access via various schemes (institutional Read & Publish agreements, Subscribe to Open, equity schemes); check eligibility for APC-free routes or discounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access discounts and membership benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors at institutions with OA Membership receive a 25% discount on OA publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check institutional OA Membership status for applicable discounts; corresponding authors at participating institutions may receive financial benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-quality copy-editing and production standards
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepted manuscripts receive professional copy-editing and production services to ensure clarity, consistency and quality in the published article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free deposit of supplementary material (Figshare)
rubrics_metrics.description: Free deposit of supplementary material (including video) in Figshare; all are fully citable
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may deposit supplementary files (data, code, video) in Figshare at no cost; deposited items receive persistent citations to support reproducibility and credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ease of submission and transfer options
rubrics_metrics.description: Ease of submission and author care: either directly to us or for some journals via BioRxiv Transfers. Transfers to Royal Society Open Science
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors can submit directly or use manuscript transfer services (e.g., from bioRxiv) and may benefit from transfer pathways between Royal Society journals to find the best fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to open science and open data
rubrics_metrics.description: A commitment to open science, open data and optional transparent peer review on some journals
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should prepare to comply with data-sharing and open-science expectations (data availability statements, repositories) and be aware of optional transparent peer review policies where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for early career researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional support and guidance for early career researchers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The publisher offers resources and guidance tailored to early career researchers (ECRs) to help with the publishing process and professional development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous constructive peer review overseen by Editorial Board
rubrics_metrics.description: Rigorous, constructive peer review overseen by an international Editorial Board of eminent scientists chaired by a Fellow of the Royal Society
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts are evaluated through a rigorous peer review process managed by an experienced editorial board; authors can expect constructive review comments and editorial oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global inclusivity and non-discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions are encouraged and welcomed from all authors, regardless of their characteristics, protected or otherwise. We are committed to equal opportunity and work diligently to mitigate bias in our editorial review processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors from any geographic or demographic background are welcome; the publisher endorses diversity and takes steps to mitigate editorial bias.
